summary: Connect CUDA/Ascend execution to native simulation, the feature-gated testbed and contract replay runners; use binary body-state readback and persistent device binary caches.
regressions: 24 native tests passed; Rust fmt/clippy, a runtime build without Metal, and the testbed build passed. Both CUDA/Ascend executable selections and launcher flags are accepted.

Nine protocol/replay regressions passed in 5.625 seconds, including binary reply framing, target rejection, iteration preservation and host-only execution through the device interface. Missing real drivers fail explicitly during preflight.
differences: CUDA/Ascend execution still needs actual hardware qualification. Driver/compiler preflight occurs before expensive scene specialization. --compare retains the existing Rust CPU reference. Native Windows remains unqualified; no GPU dependency is added to the Rust tilelang feature and no CPU physics fallback is used.
